items.title: Damon Wayans To Guest Star On NBC’s ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere In ‘In Living Color’ Reunion; First-Look Photo
items.summary:
Damon Wayans is joining NBC's St. Denis Medical for the Season 3 premiere, putting him back onscreen with his former In Living Color castmate David Alan Grier. Deadline reported the guest-starring turn along with a first-look photo from the episode.

Wayans plays Dr. Highland, described as charming and pompous in roughly equal measure, a new arrival covering for Grier's Ron while he recovers from surgery. The staff and patients take to him immediately, with the exception of Alex, which is where the comedy presumably lives.

Created by Justin Spitzer and Eric Ledgin, the workplace comedy is set at an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the staff try to treat patients without losing their minds. The ensemble includes Wendi McLendon-Covey as administrator Joyce, along with Allison Tolman, Josh Lawson, Kahyun Kim, Mekki Leeper and Kaliko Kauahi.

Season 2 followed Joyce overextending herself after a large private donation, while the rest of the hospital dealt with staff shortages and personal messes. Season 3 shifts toward romantic entanglements and personal struggles in the Emergency Department, pushing several employees to their limits.

Ledgin is showrunner and an executive producer, with Spitzer, Simon Heuer, Bridget Kyle and Vicky Luu also executive producing. Universal Television is the studio, with the series produced by More Bees, Inc. and Spitzer Holding Company.

Season 3 premieres Monday, November 2 at 8 p.m. on NBC. The first two seasons are streaming on Peacock.

items.title: Mariska Hargitay’s Best ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Episodes To Re-Air On NBC
items.summary:
NBC is clearing an evening for Mariska Hargitay ahead of her first turn as Emmy Awards host, programming a Law & Order: Special Victims Unit marathon built around three of her most acclaimed episodes. The tribute is set for Thursday, Sept. 10, according to Deadline.

The lineup runs chronologically through her Emmy history: "Charisma," a nominated episode that first aired Nov. 16, 2004, at 8 p.m.; "911," the episode that won her the 2006 Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series, at 9 p.m.; and "Undercover," another nominated episode from April 15, 2008, at 10 p.m.

Hargitay has been nominated eight times for playing Detective Olivia Benson. This year she is also up for two additional Emmys tied to My Mom Jayne, her documentary about her mother, Jayne Mansfield, in Outstanding Documentary or Non-Fiction Special and Outstanding Director for a Documentary/Non-Fiction Program. She hosts the ceremony at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles on Monday, Sept. 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT.

The Season 28 premiere is scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 8 at 9 p.m. ET/PT. Hargitay stars alongside Ice-T as Sgt. Odafin "Fin" Tutuola, with Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino, Kevin Kane and Aimé Donna Kelly also in the cast. The series will pass 600 episodes later this year.

Executive producers include Dick Wolf, Michele Fazekas, Hargitay, Ken Brown, Rebecca McGill, Anastasia Puglisi and Peter Jankowski. Universal Television produces in association with Wolf Entertainment.

items.title: Outside Lands 2026 Photo Gallery: The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese, Lucy Dacus, and More
items.summary:
Outside Lands has wrapped for another year, with San Francisco's Golden Gate Park hosting the 2026 edition of the festival. The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese and Lucy Dacus were among the acts who played across the weekend.

Consequence sent veteran concert photographer Raymond Ahner to shoot the festival, and the outlet has published his images from the grounds in a gallery covering the performances.

That is the extent of what has been reported so far: a set of photographs and a partial roster of who appeared. The full lineup and attendance figures were not included in the report.

items.title: Rufus Wainwright, Kathleen Hanna, Yo La Tengo Celebrate the Radical Music of Yoko Ono
items.summary:
A crowd gathered outside the Broad museum in Los Angeles for Yoko Only: A Night Celebrating the Music of Yoko Ono, a 19-song tribute concert staged alongside the museum's exhibition Yoko Ono: Music of the Mind. Ono, who is 93, did not attend. Yo La Tengo served as house band for most of the evening, expanded to a five-piece by Wilco's Nels Cline and Cibo Matto's Yuka Honda, who curated the program, selected the performers and often the songs, and played keyboards throughout.

The set moved across Ono's catalog without much regard for chronology or accessibility, from the free-jazz "AOS" — originally recorded in 1970 with the Ornette Coleman Quartet — to the 1981 disco single "Walking on Thin Ice" and "No, No, No," her raw response to John Lennon's murder the year before. Ira Kaplan introduced the 1973 song "What Did I Do!" by dedicating it to the Beatles, adding, "It's been long enough that we no longer bear a grudge for them trying to break up the Plastic Ono Band."

Merrill Garbus of Tune-Yards opened with "We Are All Water," updating Ono's lyrics about Chairman Mao and Richard Nixon with contemporary names. Deerhoof's Satomi Matsuzaki handled the percussive "Tabeti," Kathleen Hanna and Sleater-Kinney's Corin Tucker took on "No, No, No," and Sylvan Esso's Amelia Meath sang both "Sisters O Sisters" and "Walking on Thin Ice." Chicago duo Finom, made up of Macie Stewart and Sima Cunningham, performed "Why" and "Kiss Kiss Kiss."

Speaking backstage before the show, Tucker placed Ono at the root of her own musical generation. "Yoko Ono was just so ahead of her time and so influential to my generation, the riot grrrl generation," she said. "She was a direct influence for us of someone who was, like, no filter. Music is about expressing yourself and about being who you truly are and putting out these ideas into the world. That was a huge impact on us."

Rolling Stone's account notes that the evening's most personal contribution came from New York multimedia artist Emi Helfrich, Ono's granddaughter through her daughter Kyoko Ono Cox, who performed "Remember Love" and "Higa Noboru." Rufus Wainwright, wearing dark glasses in tribute to Ono's own, sang "I'm Going Away Smiling" — a song he said always makes him cry — with cellist Maggie Perkins, and "What a Bastard the World Is." Composer and jazz singer Theo Bleckmann took on "AOS," telling the audience, "Sing along if you like," before the piece dissolved into a noise that had listeners laughing and covering their ears.

items.title: Iceage Announce Spring 2027 North American Tour
items.summary:
Iceage have mapped out a 10-date North American headlining tour for spring 2027, supporting their album For Love of Grace & the Hereafter. The Danish punk band opens April 2nd at Neumos in Seattle and closes April 15th at Black Cat in Washington, DC.

The run threads through mid-size rooms across the continent: Aladdin Theater in Portland, The Independent in San Francisco, Teragram Ballroom in Los Angeles, Thalia Hall in Chicago, El Club in Detroit, Lee's Palace in Toronto, Bowery Ballroom in New York and The Foundry at The Fillmore in Philadelphia. Tickets go on sale Friday, August 14th at 10 a.m. local time through Ticketmaster and the band's website.

Before any of that, the band has a stack of overseas dates. Festival appearances run through August and November — including Syd For Sol in Copenhagen, Øya in Oslo, a Cologne date with Geese and Pitchfork Paris — followed by a European and UK tour from January into February that ends February 26th at Thekla in Bristol.

For Love of Grace & the Hereafter arrived in May. Consequence, which reported the tour announcement, included the record on its list of the 33 best albums of 2026 at the year's midpoint.
